title: Stocking a product line that is not cards
target: How to add tabletop games to a TCG Card Shop Simulator shop, given that the game treats a set as its own kind of stock with its own parts.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Room for a product line that is not cards
Money for a first order of sets
A shelf or display for boxed goods

steps.do: Treat a tabletop game as a set rather than as one box.
steps.because: the game keeps each one as a set with a record of its own (TableGameItemSet)

steps.do: Check what a set contains before ordering, because the parts are separate kinds.
steps.because: a play mat, a deck box and a comic book are each named parts (playMatType)

steps.do: Restock them through their own screen rather than the card list.
steps.because: tabletop games restock through a screen of their own (RestockItemBoardGameScreen)

steps.do: Put them where the sets can be seen rather than squeezing them onto a card shelf.
steps.because: each part is modelled with its own mesh (m_PlayMatMesh)

steps.do: Judge the range by the games the shop actually stocks rather than assuming one size fits.
steps.because: the game ships icons for particular games (Icon_Boardgame_Speedrobo_Mafia)

commonMistakes: Ordering a set and expecting a single box.
Shelving sets the same way as card packs.
Restocking them from the ordinary item list.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
